token_client_credentials.note: this is the catch-all clause, so it is consistent with - but does not prove - client_credentials being unimplemented. The grants implemented are read from source instead.

bearer_at_graphql_endpoint.means: the endpoint honours bearer tokens (unlike Basic, which is ignored byte-identically): a scoped OAuth access token could authenticate the write, and n8n's Header Auth credential could hold it

ics_import_route.live_schema_note: the only feed tokens are EXPORT tokens; `__type(name: "ApplicationToken")` -> null; no import*/ics* field appears in __schema

third_party_importers.ics_module: modules[] module=ical_calendar with ics_url (the example pulls a Nextcloud public calendar)

third_party_importers.README: An app to import event on a Mobilizon instance.
third_party_importers.auth: OAuth browser flow: registers a client on the instance (clientId/clientSecret fields, registerApp(), scope='read write' - app_scope.ex expands read/write to every granular scope), authorizeApp(code, clientId), grant kept in localStorage, registration routed through a hosted proxy (getProxyApiUrl('auth/register?instance=...&redirect_uri=...'))
third_party_importers.writes: createEvent, uploadMedia, createGroup (src/api/mobilizon.js); no ICS parser in package.json; src/api/scrapper.js scrapes pages; src/api/geo.js is where upstream issue !2088 lives

third_party_importers.shape: TypeScript/Node service: Dockerfile, migrations/, its own DB; README: 'crawl and import events from 3rd-party platforms and post them on Mobilizon or call webhooks ... new events are periodically checked and automatically published'; sources include ICS feeds
third_party_importers.auth: OAuth, not password: src/controllers/MobilizonOAuthController.ts + src/models/mobilizon_oauth_application.model.ts (a registered client stored per instance in its own database); src/services/mobilizon/graphql/auth.ts carries only the RefreshToken mutation
third_party_importers.writes: createEvent and updateEvent documents in src/services/mobilizon/graphql/events.ts; no deleteEvent document there
third_party_importers.read_via: GitLab API repository/tree + files/raw, ref main, 2026-11-04

ics_import_route.conclusion: no importer ships with Mobilizon; the ICS route means running a third-party app that authenticates with email+password and writes with the same createEvent, plus update/cancel/delete powers cadence does not take

bot_actors.schema: lib/mobilizon/actors/bot.ex - schema "bots": source (string), type (string, default "ics"), actor_id, user_id; table added by priv/repo/migrations/20180522133844_add_bots_table.exs
bot_actors.registration: mix mobilizon.create_bot EMAIL NAME SUMMARY TYPE URL (lib/mix/tasks/mobilizon/create_bot.ex) -> Actors.register_bot + Actors.create_bot
bot_actors.ingestion: none found in the 5.2.5-RC1 clone: grep -l Bot lib -> actors.ex, bot.ex and the mix task only; no lib/mobilizon/fetchers; lib/mobilizon/cron.ex has no bot job; no GraphQL mutation reads a bot source. So a bot is an IDENTITY an external writer can act as, not an importer
